main_text.p: cum χ, ut in ῥαχάβ. y spiritus asperrimus ope summi gutturis & narium efferendus. Graeci saepe omiserunt, ut in ἔ[?]ς, ἠ[?]αιδ &c. interdum per (γ) expresserunt, Judaei per א efferunt, quidam per (gn) vitiose.
main_text.head: SECT. 2.
De numerandi ratione.
main_text.p: Numerant Hebraei per literas Alphabeti, ut in schemate praecedente, quibus addunt pro aliis centuriis literas finales, sic ;

Vel in quinque centuriis posterioribus priores repetunt, ut [illegible, ~2 letters] 500, [illegible, ~2 letters] 600, [illegible, ~2 letters] 700, [illegible, ~2 letters] 800, [illegible, ~3 letters] 900. Post denarios addunt minores, ut יא 11. יב 12. יג 13. יד 14. at טו 15 pro יה, ne Nomen Dei prophanetur.

Millenarios sic exprimunt א 1000. בא 2000. גא 3000. דא 4000. &c. at cum centenariis compositos solummodo per אבגדה &c. ut אג ter mille, [?] 3500. saepius vero Mille voce integra per אלף exprimunt, 2000 per אלפים plura per אלפים, praemittendo literam numeralem, quot scil. millia significare volunt.

page.notes: Greek words in the first paragraph are uncertain: ῥαχάβ and the forms ἔξς and ἠσαιδ are read from a faint scan. The Hebrew finals line and the numbers 500 to 900 are clear, but the Hebrew letter groups before them are not legible enough to copy, so they are marked illegible. The Hebrew word after "ut" in the millennia sentence (אג) and the letters before "3500" are doubtful. The Hebrew in "ut אג" may be misread. The "ו" of the page is faint in places. The catchword SECT. is the start of the next section.
